title: The Truth of Ten Thousand Years Ago
next_chapter_hook: When Chen Ji stepped into the next chapter written by fate, he discovered that the so-called third path required a price he had never imagined—the lives of those he cherished most.

text.content: Dust of ten thousand years drifted slowly through the void, as if time itself had crumbled to powder before Chen Ji's eyes. He stood at the very center of fate's inscription, gazing at the flickering figure before him, shock surging in his heart like a tide. 'Chen Ji of Ten Thousand Years Ago'—this designation itself was filled with absurdity and impossibility. The Voice of Fate's inscription echoed through the empty void, each word carrying the weight of piercing through time: 'Do you know why you have come?'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji slowly raised his eyes—those eyes that usually held cowardice and humility, now terrifyingly calm. 'Why have I come?' he repeated softly, a self-mocking curve forming at the corner of his lips, 'I thought it was to survive, to seek revenge, to—' His words broke off abruptly, because some instinct told him that whatever came next would determine whether he could leave here alive.

text.content: The figure of the Voice of Fate solidified in the light, and Chen Ji finally saw the face—or rather, the face bearing seven-tenths resemblance to his own. The only difference was in the eyes of the Voice of Fate, holding a depth and vicissitude Chen Ji had never possessed, as if carrying memories and calculations spanning ten million years. 'What you see is your past self,' the Voice of Fate spoke slowly, 'and I am a fragment of consciousness projected back after breaking through the timeline.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's heart suddenly contracted, as if gripped tightly by an invisible hand. 'Consciousness fragment? Projected back?' His voice carried a tremor, but he quickly suppressed it, turning it into deeper composure. He recalled what Mo Xiansheng had said—that the holders of the Tianji Record had never been recorded as having good endings. Could the so-called 'bad ending' refer to this?

text.content: 'Simply put,' the Voice of Fate raised his hand and drew three rays of light in the void, each representing an entirely different path, 'Ten thousand years from now, you will face three choices. First, break the shackles, destroy the Tianji Record, and annihilate together with this damnable fate. Second, replace the Heavenly Way, become the new ultimate chess master, and manipulate all living beings in the palm of your hand. Third—' his voice suddenly dropped, 'Accept the cycle, repeating the same tragedy across endless timelines.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent. Each of these three paths was filled with blood and cruelty. He thought of Chen Nian's clear eyes before she disappeared, of Su Qingyao's fluttering sleeves as she practiced swordsmanship under the moonlight, of Ye Qing's solitary figure in the mists of the Demonic Path. If he chose the first path, all these people he had just come to cherish would perish alongside him. If he chose the second path—he would become the kind of person he had once despised most.

text.content: 'If you choose to replace the Heavenly Way,' the Voice of Fate's voice suddenly turned sinister, 'you will become the new ultimate chess master. But what does this mean? It means you will possess the power to manipulate the fate of all things, while also meaning—' he paused, 'the cycle will never end. Because above you, a new consciousness will be born, treating you once again as a chess piece. And the 'you' after that will face the same choice again.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed, the sound echoing through the void, carrying a hint of madness and desolation. 'So you've come to warn me?' His voice turned cold abruptly, 'A consciousness fragment that will become 'me' ten thousand years from now, standing here telling me that no matter what I choose, it's a dead end? Are you mocking my incompetence, or flaunting your identity as someone who's been through it?'

text.content: The Voice of Fate did not grow angry; instead, he regarded Chen Ji with a strange gaze, as if observing a precious treasure about to shatter. 'I came here to tell you one thing.' He took a step forward, his radiance growing more dazzling, 'The Eye of Heavenly Way chose the holder of the Tianji Record never because of their 'talent' or 'potential.' But because—' his voice dropped, 'we are all sacrifices it has selected.'

dialogue.content: 'Sacrifice?' Chen Ji's eyes suddenly contracted. He recalled Ling Yuan's vague explorations, remembered the sorrow in Mo Xiansheng's eyes whenever 'inheritance' was mentioned. So the so-called 'inheritance candidate' was merely a quota selected for death. And he, Chen Ji, from the moment he obtained the Tianji Record, had already stood upon the altar.

text.content: 'But I am different from you.' The Voice of Fate's voice suddenly became resolute, 'I struggled through ten thousand years of endless time cycles, saw through the essence of the Heavenly Way, saw through how the so-called 'fate' is merely a chess game arranged by higher beings. So I returned, to the place where everything began, wanting to change the ending.' Fire of obsession burned in his eyes, 'However, I discovered that no matter how I choose, the ending will not change—unless—'

The Voice of Fate's words broke off abruptly, as if some prohibition was preventing him from speaking the key information. Chen Ji noticed this detail, alarm bells ringing in his heart. Could this 'future self' really be trusted? Or was this another trap set by the Eye of Heavenly Way? His mind raced through various possibilities, cold sweat already seeping from his palms.

choice.prompt: Facing this truth about someone claiming to be 'himself' from ten thousand years in the future, Chen Ji needed to make a choice. He could use the Tianji Record to foresee this person's true identity, or directly question their real purpose, or choose to temporarily trust and inquire about the possibilities of the third path.

choices.text: Use the Tianji Record to Foresight the Truth
choices.description: Consume 5 Heavenly Fate points to foresee the truth or falsehood of the Voice of Fate's words over the next three hours. The cost is that one's already scarce Heavenly Fate points will leave one even more vulnerable.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial intelligence to judge whether the Voice of Fate is trustworthy
choices.risk_hint: After consuming Heavenly Fate points, one will be more passive when facing the Eye of Heavenly Way

text.content: Chen Ji hesitated no longer. His fingers quietly formed seals within his sleeve, and the fragments of the Tianji Record warmed slightly in the depths of his consciousness. Moments later, foresight images flooded his mind—he saw the flickering points in the Voice of Fate's words, and also the corners deliberately hidden. As expected, this 'future self' had not revealed the complete truth.

choices.description: Without relying on the Tianji Record, use words to probe the Voice of Fate's true intentions. Chen Ji excelled at finding flaws in dialogue, and this time was no exception.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain information through dialogue probing while not revealing one's own trump cards
choices.risk_hint: May miss crucial truth, or may be seen through by the other party

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly let out a cold laugh, arms crossed, affecting a nonchalant posture. "You claim to be my future self? Then let me ask you—if you've already seen the ending, why did you come back to stop me? Don't tell me it's for some hypocritical grand cause like 'saving all beings'—I'm not the type to believe that."

choices.description: Since the other party mentioned 'unless,' Chen Ji decided to seize on this keyword and directly inquire about the possibility of breaking the cycle, no matter how slim the hope.
choices.visible_reward: May obtain crucial information to break the cycle
choices.risk_hint: The other party may use this to further control you

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stepped forward, his burning gaze fixed on the Fate Scribe. "You just said 'unless'—unless what? Don't play riddles with me. Since you chose to appear, it can't be just to tell me a tragic story." His voice was low and firm. "Tell me, what exactly is the method to break this dead end?"

text.content: The Fate Scribe fell silent for a moment, a complex light flickering in those profound eyes. "You really are still that Chen Ji." His tone carried a hint of nostalgia. "In the endless time loop, I've witnessed your choices countless times, and every time, you ask the same question." He sighed. "But I cannot directly tell you the answer, because—"

dialogue.content: "Is it because the Eye of Heavenly Dao is watching?" Chen Ji coldly interrupted. "Or are you simply using me so you can break free from some kind of restraint? Don't forget, standing before me now, you might just be a piece in a much larger game." His words cut like a blade, piercing straight to the Fate Scribe's vital point.

text.content: The Fate Scribe's form suddenly trembled, as if struck by some painful point. "You're right." His voice turned hoarse. "I am indeed a piece—a move set in motion by you from ten thousand years ago. You sent me back to the past, to warn your past self not to repeat the same mistakes, yet—" A flash of sorrow crossed his eyes. "Every time, I fail. Because you are too much like me, and neither of us can escape the same personality flaw."

Chen Ji's heart tightened sharply. "What flaw?" he pressed. The Fate Scribe raised his head, meeting Chen Ji's gaze, and said word by word: "You trust your calculations too much, rely too heavily on the Tianji Record's foresight, yet you've forgotten—" His voice suddenly rose. "There are some variables in this world that the Tianji Record can never foresee! For example—" He stretched out his hand, pointing in some direction behind Chen Ji. "Her existence!"

dialogue.content: Chen Ji whipped his head around, following the direction the Fate Scribe was pointing. His heart nearly stopped—the direction was precisely where Chen Nian had vanished. "You mean—" His voice trembled slightly. "Nian Nian? Her existence can interfere with the Tianji Record's foresight, but can it also break this cycle?"

choice.prompt: The Fate Scribe hinted that Chen Nian might be the key to breaking the cycle. Chen Ji needs to decide his next move—whether to immediately inquire how to use Chen Nian to break the cycle, to be wary that this might be a trap, or to propose conditions demanding the other party first prove their identity.

choices.description: Chen Nian is his long-missing sister, his weakness, and his only remaining family. If his sister can truly become the key to breaking the cycle, he is willing to pay any price.
choices.visible_reward: May obtain a method to save Chen Nian and break the cycle
choices.risk_hint: May fall right into the other party's trap

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's fists clenched tightly, his knuckles turning white. "Nian Nian... She's currently in the Holy Sect's hands, as the 'Heavenly Fate Lock.'" His voice was low and dangerous. "You tell me, how can she break this cycle? With even the slightest possibility, I will trample the Holy Sect and rescue her."

choices.text: Question whether this is a trap
choices.description: Chen Ji's suspicious nature makes it impossible for him to easily trust anyone, especially this sudden apparition claiming to be his "future self." This is very likely another scheme by the Eye of Heavenly Dao.
choices.visible_reward: Probe for more clues about the other party's identity
choices.risk_hint: May provoke the other party, leading to a breakdown in dialogue

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stepped back, the light in his eyes turning ice-cold. "Interesting." A mocking curve formed at the corner of his lips. "My future self specially came back to tell me that my sister is the key to breaking the cycle? And then what? Make me risk my life to save her, only to discover this was just a scheme of yours for some purpose?" He harrumphed coldly. "Why should I believe you?"

choices.description: Chen Ji habitually takes the initiative in negotiations. He never accepts any information for free, but demands that the other party first prove they are truly his 'future self' and provide substantive assistance.
choices.visible_reward: Possibly obtain the resources and intelligence controlled by the other party

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back, his expression cold. "I don't care who you are, nor whether what you say is true or false." His voice was terrifyingly calm. "If you want me to believe you, show your sincerity. What I need most now is to improve my strength and find Nian. If you truly are 'me', you should know what's most important to me. Give me something I can use first, then we can discuss cooperation."

text.content: The Fate Chronicler watched Chen Ji's reaction, a glimmer of gratification flickering in his eyes. "You really are like me, not easily trusting anyone." He murmured softly, "Ten thousand years of cycles taught me one thing—blind trust only brings destruction. But sometimes, we need to choose to believe, otherwise we'll be trapped forever in a prison built by suspicion."

dialogue.content: He waved his hand, and a jade slip radiating soft light appeared in the air, drifting slowly toward Chen Ji. "This is all the intelligence I've gathered over ten thousand years—about the weaknesses of the Heavenly Eye, about the key to breaking the cycle, about—" His voice trembled slightly, "about Chen Nian's true identity. She's not just the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key', she is also—" The words戛然而止 again, as if some restriction was preventing him from speaking the final truth.

text.content: Chen Ji reached out and took the jade slip, but didn't examine it immediately. He stared at the Fate Chronicler, his gaze sharp as a blade. "Every time you stop right here—is it the restriction of the Heavenly Eye, or are you hiding something yourself?" His voice was ice-cold, "If you truly are me who broke through the timeline after ten thousand years, then you should know—I despise being treated as a chess piece the most. Even if that person is 'my future self'."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji decided to make the final choice—whether to accept this 'future self's' help and begin a new layout; or refuse and insist on walking his own path; or propose even more harsh conditions, demanding the other party completely stand on his side.

choices.description: Chen Ji decided to temporarily trust this 'future self', accept the intelligence within the jade slip, and cooperate with him in the layout. Though separated by ten thousand years, they were ultimately the same person, sharing common interests in opposing the Heavenly Eye.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain all intelligence collected by Chen Ji after ten thousand years
choices.risk_hint: Possibly fall into the other party's layout without realizing it

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent for a long time, then finally reached out and took the jade slip. "Fine, I'll trust you this once." His voice was calm, but dangerous light flickered in his eyes, "But if I discover you've deceived me—even if you're 'me'—I'll let you know what the counterattack of the Tianji Record feels like."

choices.description: Chen Ji decided not to rely on any 'future self'. He would break this cycle on his own. The time difference of ten thousand years meant the other party's experience might already be outdated, and he trusted his own judgment more.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain independent thinking,不被任何人操控
choices.risk_hint: Possibly miss important information, facing unknown dangers alone

dialogue.content: Chen Ji pushed the jade slip back, his gaze resolute. "Regardless of who you are, regardless of what you've experienced—that's your path, not mine." His voice was absolute, "I, Chen Ji, never walk a path arranged by others, even if that person is 'my future self'. If you want to break the cycle, figure it out yourself. My fate, I will write myself."

choices.description: Chen Ji demanded that the Fate Chronicler must completely obey his command, becoming a chess piece in his hands, rather than an equal partner. This was his instinct as a chess player—to control everything.
choices.visible_reward: Gain a powerful ally while maintaining absolute dominance
choices.risk_hint: May provoke the other party, leading to the breakdown of cooperation

dialogue.content: Chen Ji toyed with the Jade Slip in his hand, a meaningful smile curling at the corner of his mouth. "You say you've come to 'help' me?" His voice was gentle, yet carried undeniable authority. "I don't need help. What I need are chess pieces. You want to break the cycle? Fine. But from now on, you answer to me. I say east, you don't go west. So, 'future me,' are you willing to be my chess piece?"

text.content: The Fate Chronicler stared blankly at Chen Ji, as if seeing his ten-thousand-year-old self. "You truly haven't changed." He sighed softly. "In countless cycles, every time you make similar demands. Sometimes I agree, sometimes I refuse. But regardless of the outcome—" his form began to blur, "—time always returns to its origin."

dialogue.content: "Wait!" Chen Ji stepped forward, reaching out to grasp the dissolving figure. "You haven't told me yet—what is Nian Nian's true identity? What is the key to breaking the cycle? You can't just leave like this!" Rare urgency colored his voice, revealing emotions he seldom displayed.

text.content: The Fate Chronicler's voice drifted from the fading light, carrying endless vicissitudes and desolation. "Chen Ji... no, the Chen Ji from ten thousand years ago..." His form had nearly vanished, leaving only a phantom outline. "Remember, what the Heavenly Dao's Eye fears most... is not power... not wisdom... but..." His voice cut off abruptly, as if some ultimate prohibition sealed all information at the final moment.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stood motionless, watching the figure dissolve completely into the Void. His hand remained extended, long not lowered. "But what..." he murmured, his voice carrying suppressed fury. "Every time you do this, stopping at the crucial point. You think this can hook my appetite?" A cold laugh escaped him. He turned to survey the surrounding Void. "Fine, very well. Since you won't say it, I'll find out myself."

text.content: He gazed down at the Jade Slip in his palm, his fingertips gently caressing its warm, polished surface. What knowledge did this Jade Slip contain? True hope, or another meticulously crafted trap? Chen Ji didn't know. But one thing was clear to him—from this moment, his life would fundamentally change. The Chen Ji of ten thousand years past and the Chen Ji of ten thousand years future intersected at this instant. And he would write his own ending.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly raised his head, his gaze sharp as a blade, piercing deep into the Void. "Since you are me, why would you prevent me from becoming Heavenly Dao?" His voice echoed through the empty Void, carrying accusation and provocation. "If you truly are 'the me who broke through the timeline ten thousand years from now,' then you should know better than anyone—Chen Ji never plays the role of a chess piece. Either you're lying to me, or—" a dangerous smile curled at the corner of his mouth, "—you still have something you're hiding from me."

text.content: There was no response from the Void. The Fate Chronicler had completely vanished, leaving only Chen Ji alone at the intersection of time. His shadow stretched long in the faint light, as if spanning ten thousand years of time. The Jade Slip in his hand radiated gentle warmth, seemingly responding to his mood. Chen Ji took a deep breath and tucked the Jade Slip into his sleeve. He turned and walked toward the direction he came from—where Su Qingyao waited, where Chen Nian awaited rescue, where unfinished schemes still lay in wait, and where... a fate he must personally shatter awaited.
